summary: The past week saw the UAP Disclosure Forum in Washington draw attention to persistent gaps in government transparency, with panelists discussing everything from military encounters near U.S. bases to the whereabouts of missing scientists connected to classified programs. Luis Elizondo pushed back against allegations tying him to UAP secrecy efforts, while journalist Ross Coulthart called for an end to infighting that he argues is stalling progress. The centerpiece of the week may be an "Invasion of Washington" UFO tape that lawmakers are pushing to release, though some researchers warn the latest disclosure push could be a strategic dead end. New documents from AARO arrived addressing Starlink satellite correlation with UAP sightings and forced perspective effects on observations, while The Black War Department continued withholding core evaluation details on national security grounds. Meanwhile, questions about whether figures like Elon Musk have knowledge of secret programs, and concerns about legal protections for whistleblowers facing threats and retribution, underscore how institutional friction remains the central obstacle to meaningful disclosure.
